Class StyledElement<T extends StyledElement<T>>

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the concrete element type for method chaining
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
Direct Known Subclasses:
BarChartElement, CalendarElement, CanvasElement, ChartElement, Component, ContainerElement, DockElement, DualSparklineElement, FormElement, FormFieldElement, GaugeElement, GenericWidgetElement, LineGaugeElement, ListElement, MarkdownElement, MarkupTextAreaElement, MarkupTextElement, RichTextAreaElement, RichTextElement, ScrollbarElement, SparklineElement, SpinnerElement, TableElement, TabsElement, TextAreaElement, TextElement, TextInputElement, TreeElement, WaveTextElement
public abstract class StyledElement<T extends StyledElement<T>> extends Object implements Element, Styleable
Abstract base for elements that support styling and event handling. Provides a fluent API for setting colors, modifiers, and event handlers.

Implements Styleable to support CSS-based styling.

    • render

      public final void render(Frame frame, Rect area, RenderContext context)
      Renders this element. This is a template method that:
      1. Resolves the effective CSS + inline style
      2. Pushes the style and CSS resolver onto the context's stacks
      3. Calls renderContent(Frame, Rect, RenderContext) for subclass-specific rendering
      4. Pops the style and resolver when done

      Subclasses must implement renderContent(Frame, Rect, RenderContext) instead of overriding this method. The current style is available via RenderContext.currentStyle(). CSS properties not in Style (e.g., border-type) can be accessed from parent elements via DefaultRenderContext.currentResolver().

      Specified by:
      render in interface Element
      Parameters:
      frame - the frame to render to
      area - the area to render in
      context - the render context

    • resolveEffectiveStyle

      protected Style resolveEffectiveStyle(RenderContext context, String childName, Style explicitStyle, Style defaultStyle)
      Resolves a style for a sub-component following the priority: explicit > CSS > default.

      This helper method standardizes how element sub-components (like cursors, placeholders, scrollbar thumbs, etc.) resolve their styles. It enables CSS theming while preserving programmatic control when needed.

      The resolution order is:

      1. If explicitStyle is non-null, use it (programmatic override)
      2. Otherwise, check CSS via RenderContext.childStyle(String)
      3. If CSS provides styles, use those
      4. Otherwise, use defaultStyle

      Example usage in a TextInput element: 

      // In renderContent():
Style effectiveCursorStyle = resolveEffectiveStyle(context, "cursor", cursorStyle, DEFAULT_CURSOR_STYLE);
Style effectivePlaceholderStyle = resolveEffectiveStyle(context, "placeholder", placeholderStyle, DEFAULT_PLACEHOLDER_STYLE);

      This enables CSS like: 

      TextInputElement-cursor { text-style: reversed; }
TextInputElement-placeholder { color: gray; }
      Parameters:
      context - the render context for CSS resolution
      childName - the child name (e.g., "cursor", "placeholder", "thumb")
      explicitStyle - the explicitly set style (may be null for CSS/default)
      defaultStyle - the default style to use when no explicit or CSS style is set
      Returns:
      the resolved style

    • resolveEffectiveStyle

      protected Style resolveEffectiveStyle(RenderContext context, String childName, PseudoClassState state, Style explicitStyle, Style defaultStyle)
      Resolves a style for a sub-component with pseudo-class state, following the priority: explicit > CSS > default.

      Use this overload for stateful children like selected items or focused tabs.

      Example usage: 

      Style effectiveHighlightStyle = resolveEffectiveStyle(
    context, "item", PseudoClassState.ofSelected(),
    highlightStyle, DEFAULT_HIGHLIGHT_STYLE);
      Parameters:
      context - the render context for CSS resolution
      childName - the child name (e.g., "item", "row", "tab")
      state - the pseudo-class state (e.g., selected, hover), or null for none
      explicitStyle - the explicitly set style (may be null for CSS/default)
      defaultStyle - the default style to use when no explicit or CSS style is set
      Returns:
      the resolved style

    • focusable

      public T focusable()
      Makes this element focusable, allowing it to participate in TAB navigation.

      When an element is focusable:

      • It is included in the focus chain for TAB/Shift+TAB navigation
      • It receives keyboard events via handleKeyEvent(KeyEvent, boolean) when focused
      • An ID is required for focus management - if not set via id(String), one will be auto-generated at render time

      Note: focusable() and onKeyEvent(KeyEventHandler) are orthogonal:

      • Use focusable() when the element should participate in TAB navigation
      • Use onKeyEvent() to handle keyboard events (works regardless of focusability)
      • Use both when you want TAB navigation AND custom key handling
      Returns:
      this element for chaining

    • styleAttributes

      public Map<String,String> styleAttributes()
      Description copied from interface: Styleable
      Returns the style attributes for attribute selector matching.

      Attribute selectors like Panel[title="Test"] match elements based on their style attributes. This method returns a map of attribute names to their values.

      Common attributes include:

      • title - the element's title
      • label - the element's label
      • placeholder - the element's placeholder text
      Specified by:
      styleAttributes in interface Styleable
      Returns:
      an unmodifiable map of attribute names to values (never null, may be empty)

    • onKeyEvent

      public T onKeyEvent(KeyEventHandler handler)
      Sets a key event handler for this element.

      The handler receives keyboard events when:

      • This element is focused (receives events directly)
      • A focused descendant doesn't handle the event (bubbles up)

      Relationship with focusable():

      • onKeyEvent() registers a handler but does NOT make the element focusable
      • focusable() adds the element to TAB navigation but does NOT add a handler
      • Use both together when you want TAB navigation AND custom key handling
      • Use only onKeyEvent() for handling keys from focused children or global shortcuts
      Parameters:
      handler - the key event handler
      Returns:
      this element for chaining
      See Also:
      • focusable()

    • onAction

      public T onAction(ActionHandler handler)
      Sets an action handler for this element.

      This is a convenience method that dispatches both key and mouse events to the action handler. Key events are dispatched when this element is focused, mouse events when clicking on the element.

      Parameters:
      handler - the action handler to use
      Returns:
      this element for chaining

      public T on(InputTrigger trigger, Consumer<Event> handler)
      Binds an input trigger directly to a handler on this element.

      When the trigger matches an incoming event, the handler is invoked and the event is marked as handled. This bypasses the bindings/action-name system entirely, providing a direct trigger-to-handler wiring.

      Multiple on() calls compose: each call chains with the previous handler, so all registered triggers are checked in reverse registration order.

      Example: 

      text("Red").focusable()
    .on(MouseTrigger.click(), e -> color("RED"))
    .on(KeyTrigger.ch('r'), e -> color("RED"));

      Note: Calling onKeyEvent(KeyEventHandler) or onMouseEvent(MouseEventHandler) after on() replaces the chained handler, same as calling those methods multiple times.

      Parameters:
      trigger - the input trigger to match (e.g., MouseTrigger.click(), KeyTrigger.ch('r'))
      handler - the handler to invoke when the trigger matches
      Returns:
      this element for chaining
